state.name: Maryland
state.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service
state.agency_short: Maryland DNR Wildlife and Heritage Service
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May during spring raccoon and squirrel denning, spring through fall for groundhog and mole lawn work, summer for bat colonies (exclusion follows the Maryland DNR-recommended September 1 to March 1 window), and September through November as rodents and squirrels seek winter shelter
state.climate_factor: Maryland's humid subtropical summers keep snakes, groundhogs and moles active for a long season, while cold mountain winters in Garrett and Allegany counties and mild winters on the Eastern Shore produce very different intrusion calendars across one state
state.permit_note: Maryland commercial nuisance work requires a Wildlife Damage Control Permit under COMAR 08.03.15, and Maryland DNR styles its holders licensed Wildlife Damage Control Operators; mice, moles, rats and voles are exempt from the permit, relocation is allowed only in the same or an adjacent county with written release-site permission and is prohibited for raccoon, skunk and fox, and bats may be removed only by non-lethal methods under COMAR 08.03.15.20

Allegany County.region: western Maryland in the Allegheny Mountains, along the Potomac River
Allegany County.nearest_metro: Cumberland is the regional center, with Hagerstown about 65 miles east
natural_features: Wills Mountain and the Allegany ridges
Allegany County.habitat_type: mountain ridges, river towns, and former coal and canal country
Allegany County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work the older homes of Cumberland and Frostburg, groundhogs burrow the valley farms, and the mountain woods add timber rattlesnake country — safety and referral only — plus copperheads on the rocky slopes
Allegany County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel does not occur in western Maryland, and black bear problems in the Allegany woods are Maryland DNR matters, not house calls

Anne Arundel County.region: central Maryland on the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay, between Baltimore and Annapolis
Anne Arundel County.nearest_metro: Baltimore (about 25 miles north) and Washington, D.C. (about 35 miles west)
natural_features: Chesapeake Bay western shore and the Severn River
Anne Arundel County.habitat_type: state-capital waterfront, dense northern suburbs, and rural south county
Anne Arundel County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels and bats are constant in Severna Park, Pasadena and Annapolis waterfront homes with crawlspaces and boat houses, rats hold Glen Burnie's older commercial blocks, and south county farmhouses add groundhogs and black rat snakes
Anne Arundel County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel is an Eastern Shore animal and does not occur here, and osprey nests on Annapolis-area structures are protected — timing and deterrence work only

Baltimore County.region: an independent city on the Patapsco River and Baltimore Harbor, surrounded by but separate from Baltimore County
Baltimore County.nearest_metro: Baltimore is itself the metro center
natural_features: Baltimore Harbor and the Patapsco River
Baltimore County.habitat_type: dense rowhouse city with harbor, park corridors and older industrial districts
Baltimore County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are Baltimore's defining wildlife call — the rowhouse blocks, alleys and older sewers let them move building to building — with raccoons in chimneys and vacant properties, starlings and pigeons in signs and vents, and bats in older rooflines across the city
Baltimore County.absent_or_rare: Baltimore City has no groundhog or snake country of consequence inside the built city, and no armadillos occur anywhere in Maryland

Calvert County.region: southern Maryland, a peninsula between the Chesapeake Bay and the Patuxent River
natural_features: Chesapeake Bay cliffs and Calvert Cliffs State Park
Calvert County.habitat_type: rural peninsula of tobacco-farm country turned commuter exurb
Calvert County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and moles work the yards and former tobacco fields of Huntingtown and Dunkirk, raccoons and bats settle waterfront homes in Lusby and Solomons, and the county's woods add black rat snakes in barns and outbuildings
Calvert County.absent_or_rare: Calvert County's famous fossil cliffs hold no venomous-snake pattern to market — copperheads are uncommon here — and bald eagle and osprey nests are protected, deterrence only

Caroline County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore, farm country along the Choptank River
Caroline County.nearest_metro: the mid-Shore, with Easton about 20 miles west and Dover, Delaware about 30 miles northeast
natural_features: Tuckahoe Creek and Tuckahoe State Park edge
Idlewild wildlife lands and farm ponds
Caroline County.habitat_type: flat Delmarva farmland and small towns
Caroline County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs along ditch banks and barn foundations are the standing Caroline County call, raccoons work the Choptank and Tuckahoe corridors into Denton and Federalsburg attics, and farm outbuildings across the county host bats and barn owls' less welcome cousins — starlings in the vents
Caroline County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel lives in the Shore's mature pine stands and is a protected local species — referral-grade, never a removal target — and nutria in Shore marshes are a Maryland DNR eradication matter

Carroll County.region: north-central Maryland Piedmont, between Baltimore and Frederick
Carroll County.habitat_type: rolling Piedmont farm country with fast-growing southern suburbs
Carroll County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs under barns and sheds lead across Carroll's farm country, squirrels and raccoons fill Eldersburg and Westminster attics as subdivisions push into woodlots, and bats settle the older homes of Taneytown and Union Bridge
Carroll County.absent_or_rare: copperheads are uncommon in Carroll County's Piedmont and timber rattlesnakes do not occur here; both stay identification-and-safety topics, not removal marketing

Cecil County.region: northeastern Maryland at the head of the Chesapeake Bay, between Baltimore and Delaware
Cecil County.nearest_metro: Baltimore (about 55 miles southwest) and Wilmington, Delaware (about 25 miles northeast)
natural_features: Elk Neck State Park and the North East River
Chesapeake and Delaware Canal at Chesapeake City
Cecil County.habitat_type: bay-head waterfront, horse-farm country, and I-95 corridor towns
Cecil County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are steady in waterfront and canal-town homes in North East, Chesapeake City and Perryville, groundhogs work the horse farms around Fair Hill and Rising Sun, and rats follow Elkton's older blocks and the riverfront
Cecil County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel's core Maryland range is farther down the Shore; Cecil sightings are uncommon, and any fox squirrel here is treated as protected and left to Maryland DNR guidance

Charles County.region: southern Maryland along the Potomac River, Washington's exurban frontier
Charles County.nearest_metro: Washington, D.C. (about 25 miles north of Waldorf)
natural_features: Potomac River shoreline and Mattawoman Creek
Myrtle Grove and Doncaster forest lands
Charles County.habitat_type: Potomac waterfront, tobacco-farm heritage, and fast DC-exurb growth
Charles County.regional_wildlife: squirrels, raccoons and moles surge in Waldorf and La Plata's growth-era subdivisions as building pushes into pine woods, groundhogs work the Hughesville farm belt, and Potomac waterfront homes in Indian Head and Bryans Road add bats and raccoons in crawlspaces
Charles County.absent_or_rare: copperheads occur in Charles County's woods but are uncommon near homes; the county has no timber rattlesnakes, and eagle and osprey nests on the Potomac shore are protected

Dorchester County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore, the heart of Chesapeake marsh country
Dorchester County.nearest_metro: the mid-Shore, with Salisbury about 30 miles southeast
natural_features: Fishing Bay and the Honga River marshes
Dorchester County.habitat_type: the most marsh-bound county in Maryland, with working waterfronts and farm towns
Dorchester County.regional_wildlife: raccoons are the everyday Dorchester call — in Cambridge attics, Hurlock farm outbuildings and waterfront homes that sit between crabbing seasons — with skunks and opossums under the county's many raised houses and sheds, and bats in Cambridge's older stock
Dorchester County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel lives in the mature loblolly stands around Blackwater and is protected — referral-grade only — and marsh muskrats and nutria are Maryland DNR marsh-management matters, not house calls

Frederick County.region: western Maryland Piedmont and mountain county, between Washington and the Catoctins
Frederick County.nearest_metro: Washington, D.C. (about 45 miles southeast) and Baltimore (about 50 miles east)
natural_features: Catoctin Mountain Park and Cunningham Falls
Monocacy River and the Monocacy Battlefield lands
Frederick County.habitat_type: historic city, fast suburbs, and mountain and farm country
Frederick County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs are the signature Frederick County call across its farm belt, squirrels and raccoons fill Frederick City and Urbana attics, bats colonize Brunswick and Thurmont's older homes, and the Catoctin foothills add copperheads on rocky ground — protected, safety-first, never killed
Frederick County.absent_or_rare: timber rattlesnakes are a far-western Maryland mountain animal and are not a Frederick County pattern; black bear sightings at the county's mountain edge go to Maryland DNR

Garrett County.region: Maryland's far-western mountain county, the state's highest and coldest
Garrett County.nearest_metro: the Deep Creek Lake resort area anchors the county, with Cumberland about 45 miles east
Garrett County.habitat_type: high plateau, state forest, and lake resort country
Garrett County.regional_wildlife: bats and raccoons in Deep Creek Lake homes that sit closed between visits are the Garrett County staple, skunks and groundhogs work Oakland and Grantsville yards, and the Savage River woods add porcupine damage at cabins and outbuildings
Garrett County.absent_or_rare: Garrett County is Maryland's timber rattlesnake country — a protected, watchlist species handled as safety and referral only — and black bears here are common and entirely a Maryland DNR matter

Harford County.region: northeastern Maryland between Baltimore and the Susquehanna River
natural_features: Susquehanna State Park and the Susquehanna River
Bush River and Gunpowder Bay waterfront
Harford County.habitat_type: Bay waterfront, Aberdeen Proving Ground edge, and Piedmont farm country
Harford County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels and bats are constant in Bel Air, Fallston and Jarrettsville's canopy neighborhoods, rats follow the older waterfront blocks of Havre de Grace, Aberdeen and Edgewood, and farm country adds groundhogs and barn bats
Harford County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel does not occur on the western shore, and Susquehanna bald eagle concentrations are protected — observation and deterrence only

Howard County.region: central Maryland between Baltimore and Washington, built around Columbia
Howard County.nearest_metro: Baltimore and Washington, D.C. (each about 20-30 miles away)
natural_features: Patuxent River and Triadelphia Reservoir edge
Howard County.habitat_type: affluent planned suburbs, historic mill towns, and western farm country
Howard County.regional_wildlife: squirrels, raccoons and moles are the Howard County constant across Columbia, Ellicott City and Elkridge's mature suburbs, bats settle older homes in Savage and the Patapsco valley, and the western farm belt around Clarksville and Glenelg adds groundhogs and skunks
Howard County.absent_or_rare: Howard County has no venomous-snake pattern to speak of — copperheads are rare and localized — and no Delmarva fox squirrels on this side of the Bay

Kent County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore, the state's smallest county by population
Kent County.nearest_metro: the upper Shore, with Annapolis about 35 miles southwest across the Bay Bridge from neighboring Queen Anne's
natural_features: Chesapeake Bay shore at Rock Hall
Kent County.habitat_type: historic river towns, working waterfronts, and grain-farm country
Kent County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats in Chestertown's colonial-era homes and Rock Hall's waterfront houses lead Kent County's calls, groundhogs work the farm edges around Galena and Kennedyville, and skunks den under the county's many porches and sheds
Kent County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel occurs in the Shore's mature pine and hardwood stands and is protected — referral-grade only — and Eastern Neck refuge wildlife is a federal matter

Montgomery County.region: Maryland's most populous county, Washington's northern suburbs
Montgomery County.nearest_metro: Washington, D.C. (the county borders the District)
natural_features: Cabin John and the Potomac River
Montgomery County.habitat_type: dense inner suburbs, corporate corridors, and an agricultural reserve in the north
Montgomery County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels are relentless in Silver Spring, Bethesda and Takoma Park's canopy neighborhoods, rats hold the older commercial cores of Rockville, Gaithersburg and Wheaton, bats roost in the county's older colonials, and the Agricultural Reserve adds groundhogs and barn animals around Poolesville and Damascus
Montgomery County.absent_or_rare: Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve foxes and coyotes are farm-country animals, not house-call services, and the county has no timber rattlesnakes — copperheads are uncommon and localized along the Potomac

Prince George's County.region: Maryland inside the Capital Beltway and beyond, Washington's eastern suburbs
Prince George's County.nearest_metro: Washington, D.C. (the county borders the District)
natural_features: Patuxent River and the Patuxent wildlife refuge country
Greenbelt Park and the Beltsville agricultural lands
Prince George's County.habitat_type: dense Beltway suburbs, university and federal-agriculture lands, and rural south county
Prince George's County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill attics from Hyattsville and College Park to Bowie, rats are entrenched in the older Beltway-era blocks and commercial strips, bats colonize older homes in Greenbelt and Laurel, and rural south county around Upper Marlboro adds groundhogs and black rat snakes
Prince George's County.absent_or_rare: the Beltsville and Patuxent research lands hold protected species work that is federal, not residential, and no Delmarva fox squirrels occur on the western shore

Queen Anne's County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore at the Bay Bridge, Kent Island and mainland farm country
Queen Anne's County.nearest_metro: Annapolis (directly across the Chesapeake Bay Bridge)
Queen Anne's County.habitat_type: Bay Bridge commuter country, waterfront communities, and farm towns
Queen Anne's County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the Kent Island staple in waterfront homes in Stevensville, Chester and Grasonville, groundhogs and moles work Centreville and Church Hill farm edges, and mainland river towns add skunks under porches and sheds
Queen Anne's County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel lives in mature Shore pine stands including Wye Island country and is protected — referral-grade only — and osprey nests on Kent Island structures are timing and deterrence work

Somerset County.region: Maryland's southernmost Eastern Shore county, marsh and crab country
Somerset County.nearest_metro: the lower Shore, with Salisbury about 30 miles north
Somerset County.habitat_type: the state's most rural Shore county — marsh, pine woods and working waterfronts
Somerset County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work Crisfield's waterfront and Princess Anne's older homes year-round, skunks and opossums den under the raised houses and sheds that marsh country requires, and farm outbuildings across Westover and Marion host bats and starlings
Somerset County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel in the Pocomoke pine stands is protected and referral-grade only, and marsh muskrats and nutria belong to Maryland DNR marsh programs, not house calls

St. Mary's County.region: southern Maryland, Maryland's oldest county, between the Potomac and Patuxent rivers
St. Mary's County.nearest_metro: Washington, D.C. (about 60 miles northwest), with Naval Air Station Patuxent River in the county
natural_features: St. Mary's River and St. Mary's City
St. Mary's County.habitat_type: peninsula of naval-base growth, waterfront villages and Amish and farm country
St. Mary's County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels and moles surge in Lexington Park and California's growth-era subdivisions, groundhogs work the Mechanicsville and Charlotte Hall farm belt — including Amish farms — and waterfront homes from Leonardtown to Piney Point add bats and raccoons in crawlspaces
St. Mary's County.absent_or_rare: copperheads are uncommon in St. Mary's flat peninsula woods, the county has no timber rattlesnakes, and Point Lookout and river osprey and eagle nests are protected

Talbot County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore, the Bay's sailing and estate country
Talbot County.nearest_metro: the mid-Shore, with Annapolis about 40 miles west across the Bay
natural_features: Miles River and Wye River country
Chesapeake Bay shore and Tilghman Island
Talbot County.habitat_type: historic towns, waterfront estates, and farm country
Talbot County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats lead in Easton, St. Michaels and Oxford's historic homes and waterfront estates, moles and groundhogs work the farm and estate lawns, and Tilghman Island's watermen's homes add skunks and opossums under porches and sheds
Talbot County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel in the county's mature pine stands is protected and referral-grade only, and the rivers' osprey and eagle nests are protected — deterrence and timing only

Washington County.region: western Maryland's valley county, between Pennsylvania and the Potomac
Washington County.nearest_metro: Hagerstown is the regional hub, with Frederick about 25 miles east
natural_features: Antietam National Battlefield and Antietam Creek
Potomac River and the C&O Canal
South Mountain and the Appalachian Trail
Washington County.habitat_type: Hager Valley farm country, canal towns, and mountain edges
Washington County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs lead across the Hager Valley's farms and subdivisions, raccoons and bats fill Hagerstown and Boonsboro's older homes, black rat snakes work the barns around Smithsburg and Clear Spring, and South Mountain adds copperheads on rocky ground — protected and safety-first
Washington County.absent_or_rare: timber rattlesnakes are a far-western mountain animal beyond South Mountain's usual pattern and stay referral-only if ever reported; Antietam battlefield wildlife is a National Park Service matter

Wicomico County.region: Maryland's Eastern Shore commercial hub, on the Wicomico River
Wicomico County.nearest_metro: Salisbury is the lower Shore's regional center
natural_features: Pemberton Historical Park and Shore pine woods
Wicomico County.habitat_type: regional city, suburbs, and surrounding Delmarva farm and pine country
Wicomico County.regional_wildlife: rats follow Salisbury's older neighborhoods, university blocks and riverfront food businesses, raccoons and squirrels fill Fruitland and Delmar's canopy suburbs, and the surrounding farm and pine country adds groundhogs, bats in farmhouses, and Delmarva fox squirrel sightings in mature stands — protected, referral-grade only
Wicomico County.absent_or_rare: nutria in the Nanticoke marshes are a Maryland DNR eradication matter, and no venomous-snake pattern markets in Wicomico County — copperheads are rare on the lower Shore

Worcester County.region: Maryland's Atlantic coast county — Ocean City, farmland and the Pocomoke forest
Worcester County.nearest_metro: Ocean City is the resort center, with Salisbury about 30 miles northwest
natural_features: Pocomoke River and Pocomoke State Forest
Worcester County.habitat_type: barrier-island resort, coastal bays, and inland farm and forest
Worcester County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, skunks and bats are the standing job in Ocean City and Ocean Pines homes and rentals that sit empty between seasons, rats follow Ocean City's boardwalk food blocks in season, and Berlin, Snow Hill and Pocomoke City add squirrels, groundhogs and bats in older inland homes
Worcester County.absent_or_rare: the Delmarva fox squirrel in Pocomoke State Forest stands is protected and referral-grade only, Assateague's wild horses are a federal matter, and no venomous snakes market in Worcester County
